linkedin.title: We decided to stop optimizing for time spent in our app.
linkedin.body:
Most news feeds are built to keep you scrolling forever. They use engagement metrics to show you content that triggers a reaction, even if it is not actually useful to you. When we started building Headlinne, we realized that model was fundamentally broken for news.

So we changed the goal of our algorithm. Instead of maximizing your time on screen, we optimize for information density. We want you to understand the world better, not just consume more content. If you open our app, read two stories that actually matter to you, and then feel informed enough to put your phone down, we consider that a success.

This required a different engineering approach. We had to focus on relevance and summary quality rather than rage bait or clickbait. It is a harder path to build, but it is the only way to make a news product that respects your time instead of stealing it.

We believe technology should serve your curiosity, not manipulate your attention span.

story_card.headline: Turkmenistan begins fixing massive methane leaks
story_card.standfirst: The world's worst emitter of this potent greenhouse gas is finally starting repairs.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Turkmenistan has started plugging major methane leaks at its ageing oil and gas facilities.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: UN data recently exposed the country as the world's worst offender for these mega-leaks.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas. Stopping these leaks is a huge win for the climate.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Whether these repairs continue across all facilities to sustain this breakthrough.

story_card.caption:
Turkmenistan has started repair work to stop the massive methane leaks coming from its oil and gas infrastructure.

For years, the secretive nation has been the leading source of these harmful emissions. New UN data indicates that maintenance is finally underway at their ageing sites. This marks a significant environmental shift for the country.
